name: subagent-session-isolation
body:
The session-lifecycle policy that governs how the `codebase-navigator` (the coordinator actor, `requirements.user.navigator-agent`) uses the `subagent` tool: a dispatch is a fresh, isolated subagent session, one dispatch is one self-contained unit of work, and each task runs in its own dispatch. The single permitted resume is the within-dispatch hand-back loop — the subagent returns needing a navigator action (a scan, a quick verify, an `apg_review_action`), the navigator performs it, and resumes that same session to finish the same task (the mark-done step) before ending it. That resume is confined to the same dispatch: it finishes the task in hand, and resumption across tasks or phases is outside the policy; each review round runs as a fresh dispatch.

The policy bounds resumption to the one hand-back loop. Subagent context (the context window of a resumed session) is finite, and repeated resumption across tasks and phases accumulates context until the subagent breaks, so isolation is the design. The policy refines `domain.entity.task-execution-cadence`'s "resumes the session only to mark done" step by naming the one permitted resume: the cadence names the ordering for mutating the plan (commit → quick verify → scan → resume to mark done), while this entity confines that resume to the same dispatch. The navigator prompt (`solution.component.codebase-navigator-prompt`) states it and the coherence test (`solution.component.navigator-isolation-coherence-test`) pins it.
